lesson.title: Data protection by design and by default
lesson.summary: Build the principles into systems from the start, and choose privacy-friendly default settings.

prerequisites.reason: Pseudonymisation is the example measure Article 25 names.
Article 25 is a duty of the controller, decided when it chooses the means.
Design measures implement principles such as minimisation.

blocks: **Data protection by design** (Article 25(1)): the controller must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures that are designed to implement the data protection principles effectively, and must integrate the necessary safeguards.
Article 25(1) names **pseudonymisation** as an example measure and **data minimisation** as an example principle.
This applies **both** at the time the means of processing are decided **and** at the time of the processing itself (Article 25(1)).
It is about planning before you build or buy, not fixing things afterwards.
What is appropriate depends on the state of the art, the cost of implementation, the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing, and the risks.
**Data protection by default** (Article 25(2)): by default, only the personal data **necessary for each specific purpose** may be processed. This covers four dimensions:
In particular, by default personal data must not be made accessible to an **indefinite number of people** without the individual's own intervention (Article 25(2)).
An approved certification can be used as one element to demonstrate compliance with Article 25 (Article 25(3)).

items: The date-of-birth field is removed. That is design, implementing minimisation.
Optional fields start empty, and marketing is unticked. These are defaults.
Order data is deleted automatically after a set period, which handles storage by default.
A new "top customers" leaderboard is **off** unless a customer switches it on, which limits accessibility by default.
Shop staff see only the orders for their own shop, which limits access.

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.

questions.prompt: Sunfield adds a public leaderboard of top customers by name. What must the default be?

options.blocks: On, as long as the notice mentions it
options.reason: A notice does not replace a privacy-friendly default.

options.blocks: Off, until a customer chooses to join
options.reason: Article 25(2): not accessible to an indefinite number without the person's intervention.

options.blocks: On, with an option to opt out
options.reason: Opt-out exposes people without their intervention.

questions.prompt: Which dimensions does the by-default rule in Article 25(2) cover?

options.blocks: Amount, extent of processing, storage period and accessibility
Only the amount of data collected
Only the security of the data
options.reason: Security is Article 32. Article 25(2) concerns necessity.
